ideas.risks: Could stall if all candidate theorems require weak-learner returns confidence/margin or sample-dependent weights not available from 0/1 excess-risk oracle; constants may still hide inverse-polynomial-in-gap terms that make the round complexity non-polynomial in 1/ε.
ideas.summary: Produce a one-page exact translation from the atlas oracle `err_D(h) ≤ OPT_C(D)+β` to fixed `(α,γ)` assumptions in KMV08 / Feldman / potential-based agnostic boosting results, including theorem numbers, norm convention conversions, and runtime dependence on `1/(1/2-β)` and `1/ε`; identify which theorem, if any, already implies target for this exact interface.
ideas.title: Close the oracle-semantics gap with explicit theorem map
ideas.why_promising: This is the highest-uncertainty blocker; either a known theorem instantly settles the edge or it sharply proves a missing assumption (instead of heuristic optimism).

ideas.risks: Requires constructing an explicit `(C,D,F)` with heavy quantifier bookkeeping; may be impossible for natural classes unless extra constraints are allowed; construction might also accidentally rely on complexity assumptions not yet in place.
ideas.summary: Formalize a concrete `C,D` where any admissible clipping/residual wrapper (including `idea_01` style) is forced to encounter either `OPT_C(D_t)→1/2` or exponentially fast mass collapse in polynomially many rounds, with fully quantified guarantees and explicit dependence on β.
ideas.title: Build a quantified obstruction witness for adaptive filters
ideas.why_promising: A definitive negative route would instantly settle the edge (or at least this wrapper family) and prevent chasing infeasible positive invariants.

ideas.risks: May only yield conditional impossibility under SQ/hardness assumptions not matching standard agnostic learnability definitions; finite-precision bounds could be too weak to rule out all algorithms not simulable by SQ.
ideas.summary: Formalize the fixed-slack weak-agnostic learner as an oracle with bounded tolerance/precision (from `0/1` excess-risk output and sample access) and attempt an amplification lower bound showing arbitrary-ε cannot be achieved without extra oracle information or assumptions.
ideas.title: SQ-precision amplification barrier under fixed slack
ideas.why_promising: If successful, this gives a principled negative explanation for the apparent fixed-accuracy floor and guides where positive results must add assumptions.

ideas.risks: Need to identify the right stability condition strong enough to be useful yet broad enough to hold for nontrivial classes; risk of ending with a theorem too narrow to be meaningful and already known.
ideas.summary: Investigate subclasses where Route A becomes provable: e.g., bounded noise/margin/noise-agnostic conditions, margin-based low-density assumptions, or classes with one-sided noise and Tsybakov-like margin; prove the edge there with explicit computable `γ_t` bounds.
ideas.title: Conditional positive theorem under explicit stability/noise assumptions
ideas.why_promising: Keeps project productive by delivering a credible theorem-grade result even if general edge remains open; fits current conjectural notes and can produce sharp, publishable conditional statements.

ideas.risks: May reduce to known minimax impossibility if fixed-margin estimators are too weak; proving variance control may require new concentration tools for adaptively weighted samples.
ideas.summary: Design a computable wrapper that explicitly tracks `γ_t` from empirical residual statistics with confidence calibration at each round, and prove invariants with online concentration under adaptive sampling, focusing on polynomial lower bounds for both acceptance mass and gap estimates.
ideas.title: Make `γ_t` directly estimable under adaptive reweighting
ideas.why_promising: This addresses the critical open technical gap flagged repeatedly: without estimable certificates, positive invariants are not computationally meaningful regardless of existential proofs.
